units.source_text: 日文“云隐”是“隐遁”之意，乃暗示源氏之死。

en.t: The Japanese title Kumogakure means seclusion, and it hints at Genji's death.

units.source_text: 这一回只有题名而无本文，因此源氏何时死去亦不可知。

en.t: This chapter has only a title and no text, so it is also impossible to know when Genji died.

units.source_text: 但可推测如下：次回“匂皇子”（匂是日本人造的汉字，其发音为niou。

en.t: But the matter can be inferred as follows: in the next chapter, Niou no Miya, the character niou is a kanji created in Japan, and its pronunciation is niou.

units.source_text: 意义是香）中所述的是上回“魔法使”以后八年的事，

en.t: Its meaning is fragrance, and what is described there takes place eight years after the previous chapter, The Wizard.

units.source_text: 而篇首说“光源氏逝世之后……”，可知源氏是在“魔法使”的次年五十三岁至六十岁的八年之间死去的。

en.t: Since the opening says, after Hikaru Genji passed away, we can tell that Genji died sometime during the eight years from the year after The Wizard, when he was fifty-three, until he was sixty.

units.source_text: 究竟哪一年死，不得而知。

en.t: Exactly which year he died cannot be known.

units.source_text: 但第四十九回“寄生”中说：“最后二三年间遁世时所居的嵯峨院……”，

en.t: However, chapter forty-nine, Parasitic Vine, says, the Saga retreat where he lived in seclusion during his final two or three years.

units.source_text: 则可知五十三岁之后，曾隐居在预先建造的嵯峨佛堂（见“赛画”“松风”）中二三年，然后死去。

en.t: From this we know that after the age of fifty-three, he spent two or three years in seclusion at the Saga Buddhist hall he had built in advance, as seen in The Picture Contest and Matsukaze, and then died.

units.source_text: 其卒年至早是五十五六岁。

en.t: The earliest he could have died was at fifty-five or fifty-six.

units.source_text: 本回题名“云隐”，便是暗示这二三年的隐遁的。

en.t: The title of this chapter, Kumogakure, is meant to hint at those two or three years of seclusion.

units.source_text: 关于有题名而无本文的原因，自来有四种说法：

en.t: As for why there is a title but no text, four explanations have long been offered.

units.source_text: 一、本来有本文，后来因故损失；

en.t: First, there was originally a text, but it was later lost for some reason.

units.source_text: 二、作者本拟写本文，因某种缘故而作罢；

en.t: Second, the author originally intended to write the text, but gave it up for some reason.

units.source_text: 三、作者故意不写本文，听其空白；

en.t: Third, the author deliberately did not write the text and left it blank.

units.source_text: 四、本来连题名也没有，更不用说本文。

en.t: Fourth, there was originally not even a title, let alone any text.

units.source_text: 千年以来，学者各持一说，无有定论。

en.t: For a thousand years, scholars have each upheld their own view, and no settled conclusion has been reached.

units.source_text: 但普通都相信第三说，理由是：书中已描述了许多人的死，

en.t: But the third explanation is generally believed, because the book has already described the deaths of many people.

units.source_text: 其中主要人物紫夫人之死，描写得尤为沉痛。

en.t: Among them, the death of the major character Lady Murasaki is depicted with particular grief.

units.source_text: 倘再续写主人公源氏之死，这位青年女作者不堪其悲。

en.t: If she had gone on to write the death of the protagonist Genji as well, this young female author could not have borne the sorrow.

units.source_text: 因此只标题目而不写本文，借以向读者暗示此意。

en.t: Therefore she provided only the title and did not write the text, using this to suggest the meaning to the reader.
